data.narrative:
Lumafield is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $142M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-matched companies Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy anchor of $10M and applying a 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier, implies a $17M valuation. The Peer-Median method, grounded in 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables, yields a $1.0B median with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The wide dispersion between these methods reflects material uncertainty: the stage-progression approach understates typical Series C robotics valuations, while peer comparables suggest substantially higher values reflecting market dynamics in frontier manufacturing.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $14M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $508M. The magnitude of this spread reflects fundamental disagreements about how to weight capital-efficiency models versus peer trading multiples in an emerging sector. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Lumafield's product-market fit and customer traction match or diverge from peer cohort benchmarks, and whether the peer set adequately represents market conditions at the time of this valuation.
